I am an old man now, 67 years, and I have farmed this land in Nsanje all my life. This season I am planting sorghum because the rains here are not reliable and the heat is strong — sorghum does not fail me like maize sometimes does. I do not have money for fertilizer from the shop, and the coupon from the government usually goes to those planting maize, not sorghum. I will put some manure from my goats and chickens on the plot, use the seed I kept from last year's harvest, and work the land myself with help from my wife and grandchildren.
